traditionalDress.men: Dhoti-kurta or kurta-pajama for everyday and festive wear; a sherwani is worn for formal or ceremonial occasions, particularly in the Awadh (Lucknow) region.
traditionalDress.women: Sarees and salwar kameez, frequently featuring Lucknow's Chikankari (delicate hand embroidery) or woven from Banarasi silk, prized for its gold brocade work.

festivals.name: Kumbh Mela
festivals.description: One of the world's largest religious gatherings, held at Prayagraj at the confluence of the Ganges, Yamuna, and mythical Saraswati rivers, where pilgrims bathe to seek spiritual purification.

festivals.name: Ram Barat
festivals.description: A grand procession in Ayodhya reenacting the wedding of Lord Rama, featuring decorated floats, music, and dance.

festivals.name: Braj Holi
festivals.description: An extended Holi celebration in Mathura and Vrindavan honoring Lord Krishna, including the distinctive Lathmar Holi, in which women playfully beat men with sticks.

folklore: The Alha-Khand, an oral epic from the Bundelkhand region (spanning parts of Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh), celebrates the 12th-century warrior brothers Alha and Udal, who fought under King Parmal of Mahoba; sung for over 900 years by folk balladeers, it remains part of an annual festival in Mahoba tied to the monsoon season.
